rv.q: It is a painting, probably by the impressionist master Camille Pissarro, and also probably stolen from a Jewish household whose members perished in a concentration camp during the second world war. The siblings don’t know how it got here but suspect it was swiped by their grandfather – a medalled war hero who served on the German front.
Relics, artfully staged on Joanna Scotcher’s living room set, is always entertaining, if not quite a triumph.
Full-blooded production of an undernourished play
Instead, the production tries to do both in tandem – big idea thinking and slapstick comedy – and swiftly goes off the rails.
This is intelligent, wildly entertaining theatre.
The humour is creative, the story believable and substantial, the cast perfectly matched, and the direction is impeccable.
Relics is terrific entertainment that is also about something urgent and relatable.
This is a beautifully realised production, full of comic details, delicate characterisation and OTT set pieces.
At its core, Relics is ultimately a nostalgic celebration of sibling connections: their intimacies, resentments, loyalties, and ever-lasting bonds.
While sufficiently entertaining, there was still the unshakeable feeling that this was very, very well-trodden ground.
As it stands, this version of Relics needs a substantial rewrite.
A brilliantly written dramedy that balances humour, grief and uncomfortable truths with remarkable skill.
This is a compelling, vividly detailed and realistic family drama which looks into the heart of how what binds us together is also what can pull us apart.
Phillips's portrayal of Olivia stands out, as she drives the emotional backbone of the story with passion.
Sadly, the slow reveal of the characters and their motivations takes too long to develop, making it difficult to invest in them and their predicament.

Relics doesn’t always quite know where it wants to take the characters or what the outcome of the central dispute should be, but many will recognize and enjoy the petty family squabbles and the inability to ever shake off the formative past you have shared with your siblings.
The entire production of Relics is a delight – catch it while you can!

cn.t: This dark family comedy about siblings dividing their deceased mother's estate earns mixed-to-positive reviews. Critics praise the sharp writing and strong performances, but some find the plot-driven drama undermines character development.
